```{r}
#| label: setup

# In a real study, these would typically be loaded via a site-wide .Rprofile

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)      # kable() — basic tables
```

# Introduction

This report summarises the **demographics** and **adverse event** profile
for Study XYZ-001, a Phase II randomised controlled trial comparing
**Drug A** versus **Placebo** in adult subjects with condition Z.

> **Note for programmers:** This document is a single `.qmd` source file.
> The tables, figures, and narrative are produced from the same R code
> every time the document is rendered — no copy-paste from SAS output.

---

# Data

## Create Fictional Datasets

In a real study environment these datasets would be read from SAS transport
files (`.xpt`) or from a validated ADaM data store on the clinical network.
Here we create small fictional datasets inline so the example is
**fully self-contained**.

```{r}
#| label: create-adsl

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# ADSL  —  Subject-Level Analysis Dataset (one row per subject)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(42)   # reproducibility — equivalent to SAS options SEED=42

n <- 60

adsl <- tibble(
  USUBJID = paste0("XYZ-001-", sprintf("%03d", 1:n)),
  TRT01P  = rep(c("Drug A", "Placebo"), each = n / 2),      # treatment arm
  AGE     = c(rnorm(n / 2, mean = 52, sd = 11),
              rnorm(n / 2, mean = 50, sd = 10)) |> round(),
  SEX     = sample(c("M", "F"), n, replace = TRUE,
                   prob = c(0.55, 0.45)),
  RACE    = sample(
              c("WHITE", "BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN", "ASIAN", "OTHER"),
              n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.65, 0.15, 0.12, 0.08)
            ),
  WEIGHTBL = round(rnorm(n, mean = 78, sd = 14), 1),         # kg at baseline
  SAFFL   = "Y"                                              # safety flag
)

# Quick sanity check — like PROC FREQ in SAS
count(adsl, TRT01P)
```

```{r}
#| label: create-adae

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# ADAE  —  Adverse Event Analysis Dataset (one row per AE per subject)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
ae_terms <- c(
  "Headache", "Nausea", "Fatigue", "Dizziness",
  "Rash", "Vomiting", "Insomnia", "Back pain"
)

# Drug A subjects have slightly higher AE rates (fictional)
adae <- bind_rows(
  # Drug A
  tibble(
    USUBJID = sample(adsl$USUBJID[adsl$TRT01P == "Drug A"], 45, replace = TRUE),
    AETERM  = sample(ae_terms, 45, replace = TRUE),
    AESEV   = sample(c("MILD", "MODERATE", "SEVERE"), 45,
                     replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.60, 0.30, 0.10)),
    AEREL   = sample(c("RELATED", "NOT RELATED"), 45,
                     replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.55, 0.45))
  ),
  # Placebo
  tibble(
    USUBJID = sample(adsl$USUBJID[adsl$TRT01P == "Placebo"], 30, replace = TRUE),
    AETERM  = sample(ae_terms, 30, replace = TRUE),
    AESEV   = sample(c("MILD", "MODERATE", "SEVERE"), 30,
                     replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.70, 0.25, 0.05)),
    AEREL   = sample(c("RELATED", "NOT RELATED"), 30,
                     replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.60))
  )
) |>
  left_join(select(adsl, USUBJID, TRT01P), by = "USUBJID")

nrow(adae)
```

---

# Demographics Summary {#sec-demog}

The table below mirrors what you would produce in SAS with `PROC TABULATE`
or `PROC REPORT`. Here it is built with `dplyr` and rendered with `kable()`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-demog
#| tbl-cap: "Table 1. Subject Demographics and Baseline Characteristics (Safety Population)"

# Helper: mean (SD) formatter
mean_sd <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))

# Helper: n (%) formatter
n_pct <- function(x, total) sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(x), 100 * sum(x) / total)

n_by_trt <- count(adsl, TRT01P) |>             # named vector of N per arm
  { \(d) setNames(d$n, d$TRT01P) }()

demog_rows <- bind_rows(
  # Age
  adsl |>
    group_by(TRT01P) |>
    summarise(value = mean_sd(AGE), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = TRT01P, values_from = value) |>
    mutate(Characteristic = "Age (years), mean (SD)", .before = 1),

  # Weight
  adsl |>
    group_by(TRT01P) |>
    summarise(value = mean_sd(WEIGHTBL), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = TRT01P, values_from = value) |>
    mutate(Characteristic = "Weight at baseline (kg), mean (SD)", .before = 1),

  # Sex
  adsl |>
    group_by(TRT01P) |>
    summarise(value = n_pct(SEX == "F", n()), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = TRT01P, values_from = value) |>
    mutate(Characteristic = "Female, n (%)", .before = 1),

  # Race — White
  adsl |>
    group_by(TRT01P) |>
    summarise(value = n_pct(RACE == "WHITE", n()), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = TRT01P, values_from = value) |>
    mutate(Characteristic = "  White, n (%)", .before = 1),

  # Race — Black
  adsl |>
    group_by(TRT01P) |>
    summarise(value = n_pct(RACE == "BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN", n()), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = TRT01P, values_from = value) |>
    mutate(Characteristic = "  Black or African American, n (%)", .before = 1),

  # Race — Asian
  adsl |>
    group_by(TRT01P) |>
    summarise(value = n_pct(RACE == "ASIAN", n()), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = TRT01P, values_from = value) |>
    mutate(Characteristic = "  Asian, n (%)", .before = 1)
)

kable(
  demog_rows,
  col.names = c(
    "Characteristic",
    paste0("Drug A (N=", n_by_trt["Drug A"], ")"),
    paste0("Placebo (N=", n_by_trt["Placebo"], ")")
  ),
  align = c("l", "c", "c")
)
```

# Adverse Events {#sec-ae}

## AE Incidence by Treatment Arm

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ae-incidence
#| tbl-cap: "Table 2. Subjects with Any Adverse Event by System Organ Class and Preferred Term"

ae_summary <- adae |>
  distinct(USUBJID, TRT01P, AETERM) |>       # one row per subject-PT
  group_by(TRT01P, AETERM) |>
  summarise(n_subj = n_distinct(USUBJID), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(
    count(adsl, TRT01P) |> rename(N = n),
    by = "TRT01P"
  ) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n_subj / N, 1),
         cell = paste0(n_subj, " (", pct, "%)")) |>
  select(AETERM, TRT01P, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = TRT01P, values_from = cell, values_fill = "0 (0.0%)") |>
  arrange(AETERM)

kable(
  ae_summary,
  col.names = c(
    "Adverse Event (Preferred Term)",
    paste0("Drug A (N=", n_by_trt["Drug A"], ")"),
    paste0("Placebo (N=", n_by_trt["Placebo"], ")")
  ),
  align = c("l", "c", "c")
)
```

## AE Severity Profile

The figure below is produced inline by R — no external image file needed.
In SAS you would export an ODS Graphics PNG and link it manually.
Here the plot is part of the reproducible document.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ae-severity
#| fig-cap: "Figure 1. Adverse Event Counts by Severity and Treatment Arm"
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 7

adae |>
  count(TRT01P, AESEV) |>
  mutate(
    AESEV = factor(AESEV, levels = c("MILD", "MODERATE", "SEVERE"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = AESEV, y = n, fill = TRT01P)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Drug A" = "#2166ac", "Placebo" = "#d1e5f0")) +
  labs(
    x = "Severity",
    y = "Number of AEs",
    fill = "Treatment",
    title = "Adverse Events by Severity Grade"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Inline R Values in Narrative Text

One of Quarto's most powerful features for clinical programming:
values computed in R can be embedded directly in prose.

> A total of **`r nrow(adsl)`** subjects were included in the Safety Population:
> **`r n_by_trt["Drug A"]`** in the Drug A arm and
> **`r n_by_trt["Placebo"]`** in the Placebo arm.
> Across both arms, **`r n_distinct(adae$USUBJID)`** subjects
> (`r round(100 * n_distinct(adae$USUBJID) / nrow(adsl), 1)`%)
> experienced at least one adverse event.

If the data change upstream and you re-render, **every number updates automatically**.
No more manual edits after an unblinding data cut.

---

# Key Takeaways for SAS Programmers

| SAS concept | Quarto / R equivalent |
|---|---|
| `ODS RTF` / `ODS PDF` | Change `format:` in YAML header |
| `%include 'setup.sas'` | `source("_setup.R")` or `library()` |
| `PROC REPORT` / `PROC TABULATE` | `dplyr` + `kable()` / `gt` / `flextable` |
| `ODS Graphics` | `ggplot2` — inline, no external file |
| Hard-coded counts in text | `` `r nrow(adsl)` `` — live inline values |
| Manual re-run after data cut | `quarto render` — full refresh in one command |

# Appendix: Session Info {.appendix}

Good practice: capture the R environment for reproducibility traceability —
equivalent to logging SAS version and macro versions.

```{r}
#| label: session-info
#| echo: false

si <- sessionInfo()
cat(paste("R version:", si$R.version$version.string), "\n")
cat(paste("Platform:", si$R.version$platform), "\n")
cat("Key packages loaded:\n")
pkgs <- c("dplyr", "ggplot2", "knitr", "tidyr")
for (p in pkgs) {
  cat(sprintf("  %s %s\n", p, packageVersion(p)))
}
cat(paste("\nRendered:", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z")))
```
